proof.text: Construct the quotient presentation of the restricted closed immersion by the ring first isomorphism theorem: its affine section map is surjective and has kernel i.ker.ideal U. Apply affine_quotient_restricted_iso to obtain arbitrary target coefficient coordinates. For the source compose restrictUnitIso with the restriction of tildeSelf.

The canonical coefficient map is locally surjective: around any point choose an affine open inside the given open, then lift the restricted target section through i.app_surjective. The sheaf locally-surjective criterion makes it epic. The hypothesis ha identifies a with this canonical map. Restriction along an open immersion preserves epimorphisms.

The tilde functor followed by restriction along the affine chart is fully faithful, since chart restriction is an equivalence. Pull the transported epic coefficient morphism back to an A-linear map f:A → A/I. Faithfulness reflects epimorphisms, so f is surjective. A-linearity gives f(x) = (x mod I) f(1). Surjectivity supplies x with f(x)=1, making f(1) a unit. Compose the target coordinates with multiplication by its inverse. The resulting f is precisely the quotient map. Mapping this equality through T and cancelling the source-coordinate isomorphism proves the requested square. All steps apply also to the zero quotient and empty charts.

title: Affine closed immersion coefficient square

lean.statement:
theorem affine_closedImmersion_coefficient_square
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (U : Y.affineOpens)
    (a : SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf ⟶
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf))
    (ha : a = (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction i).unit.app _ ≫
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).map (Scheme.Modules.pullbackObjUnitIso i).hom) :
    let A := (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u)
    let I := i.ker.ideal U
    let T := tilde.functor Γ(Y, U.1) ⋙ Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.2.isoSpec.hom
    let R := Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.1.ι
    ∃ (eO : R.obj (SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf) ≅ T.obj (ModuleCat.of A A))
      (eB : R.obj ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)) ≅ T.obj (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I))),
      R.map a ≫ eB.hom = eO.hom ≫ T.map (ModuleCat.ofHom I.mkQ)

statement: Let i:Z → Y be a closed immersion, U an affine open of Y, A=Γ(Y,U), I=ker(i)(U), R restriction to U, and T associated sheafification followed by the affine chart transport. For the actual pullback-pushforward adjunction unit coefficient map a:O_Y → i_*O_Z there exist eO:R(O_Y) ≅ T(A) and eB:R(i_*O_Z) ≅ T(A/I) such that R(a) followed by eB equals eO followed by T of the quotient map. These are coefficient-object identifications; no Koszul complex or homology is involved. Schemes and closed immersions are those of [def-pc-scheme] and [def-weil-closed-immersion]; I is evaluated from [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and associated module sheaves use [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections].
